plan.contextChunk: This figure shows two doubly linked lists and a free list sharing one set of arrays, drawn as a shaded three-row table beside three head pointers. At the left, three labeled boxes give the heads: "free" in a black box holding a white 10, "L2" in a medium gray box holding 9, and "L1" in a light gray box holding 3. To the right sits a black panel with columns numbered 1 through 10 across the top and three rows labeled in italics down the left side: next, key, prev. Every occupied cell is shaded to match the list that owns it. The medium gray cells at indices 9, 7, 1, and 5 carry keys k9, k7, k1, and k5, their next entries reading 7, 1, 5, and a diagonal slash for nil, their prev entries reading slash, 9, 7, and 1. The light gray cells at 3, 6, and 2 hold k3, k6, and k2, with next entries 6, 2, slash and prev entries slash, 3, 6. The black slots at 4, 8, and 10 hold only next values, 8, a slash, and 4, their key and prev cells left empty and cut by dotted white rules. Shading alone separates three structures interleaved across the same index range, and the free chain 10, 4, 8 shows that a slot on the free list needs just one link.

interactionPlan.concept: Several doubly linked lists and a free list can share one set of index-parallel arrays (next, key, prev), with each object being just a slot index and allocation/freeing being pointer surgery on the free chain rather than data movement.
elements: Left column of three head-pointer boxes, each a labeled square: italic 'free' label with a black box containing white '10'; italic 'L2' label with a medium-gray box containing '9'; italic 'L1' label with a light-gray box containing '3'
Main black rectangular panel representing the shared storage arrays
Column index header row above the panel: numbers 1 through 10, evenly spaced, black text on white background
Three italic row labels to the left of the panel: 'next', 'key', 'prev'
Row 'next' cells: 1→5, 2→nil slash, 3→6, 4→8 (white text on black), 5→nil slash, 6→2, 7→1, 8→nil slash (white diagonal on black), 9→7, 10→4 (white text on black)
Row 'key' cells: 1→k1, 2→k2, 3→k3, 5→k5, 6→k6, 7→k7, 9→k9; indices 4, 8, 10 empty/black
Row 'prev' cells: 1→7, 2→6, 3→nil slash, 5→1, 6→3, 7→9, 9→nil slash; indices 4, 8, 10 empty/black
Medium-gray shading on cells of indices 9, 7, 1, 5 (list L2)
Light-gray shading on cells of indices 3, 6, 2 (list L1)
Black (unshaded) slots at indices 4, 8, 10 belonging to the free list, with only a next value
Dotted white horizontal rules cutting across the unused key and prev cells of free-list slots 4, 8, 10
Diagonal slash glyph used as the nil marker in next and prev cells
Legend/annotation strip mapping shade → structure: light gray = L1, medium gray = L2, black = free list
Curved highlight arrows (drawn on demand) from a next cell to the head of the referenced column, and from a prev cell back to its referenced column

interactions.teaches: That three independent linked structures are interleaved across the same index range: following one head pointer through its next fields visits only its own shade, skipping over slots owned by the other lists.
That a number inside a next or prev cell is not data but an index — hovering lights up the column it points at (or marks it nil), making the pointer semantics of the compact table explicit.
That ALLOCATE-OBJECT pops the head of the free chain and FREE-OBJECT pushes a slot back, so records are never copied — only next, key, and prev entries and the head pointers change.
interactions.label: Allocate / Free

interactions.teaches: That the same free slot can be recycled into either list, showing that ownership is expressed purely by which list's pointers reach it.

demo_steps.title: One table, three structures
demo_steps.narration: The black panel is a single set of parallel arrays indexed 1 to 10. Shading is the only thing distinguishing three separate structures living inside it: light gray for L1, medium gray for L2, and black for the free list.

demo_steps.title: Trace L1
demo_steps.narration: Click the L1 head box (3): the trace lights slot 3, then next[3]=6, then next[6]=2, then nil. The chain jumps over slots 4 and 5 because those belong to other structures.

demo_steps.title: Trace L2 and read prev
demo_steps.narration: Click L2 (head 9) to follow 9 → 7 → 1 → 5 → nil, then hover any prev cell to see the backward arrow: prev[1]=7 points exactly where next[7]=1 came from, confirming the list is doubly linked.

demo_steps.title: The free list needs only one link
demo_steps.narration: Click the free head (10) to follow 10 → 4 → 8 → nil. The key and prev rows of these slots are struck out with dotted rules — a free slot carries no data and needs no back pointer.

demo_steps.title: Allocate a slot
demo_steps.narration: Press allocate: slot 10 is popped off the free chain, free is reset to 4, and slot 10 is spliced onto the front of L1 — only next[10], prev[3], key[10] and the two head pointers change color and value.

demo_steps.title: Free it again
demo_steps.narration: Press free: slot 10 is unlinked from L1, its key and prev are struck out again, next[10] is set to the old free head, and free points back at 10. No record ever moved in memory.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: An 'object' here is nothing but an index — so allocation and deallocation are just relinking next pointers between a shaded list and the free chain, and multiple lists can coexist in one array because shading (ownership) is defined entirely by which chain reaches a slot.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Horizontal layout: a narrow left column of three stacked head-pointer boxes (free = black box with white 10, L2 = medium-gray box with 9, L1 = light-gray box with 3, each with an italic serif label to its left), and a wide black array panel to the right. Above the panel, column indices 1–10 in plain serif numerals. Down the panel's left edge, italic labels next, key, prev for the three rows. Cells are tall narrow rectangles; occupied cells are filled light gray (L1: 3, 6, 2) or medium gray (L2: 9, 7, 1, 5) with dark text; free slots (4, 8, 10) stay black with white text and only a next value, their key/prev cells crossed by dotted white horizontal rules. Nil is drawn as a diagonal slash matching the cell's text color. Keys render as k with a subscript index. Highlight state should use a saturated accent (e.g. orange/amber) outline plus curved arrows arcing above the table from a next cell to the top of the target column, and below the table for prev. Keep the overall tone grayscale so that the accent color reads as 'currently traced'.

discrepancies: A cluster of stray, overlapping glyphs is rendered at the top-left corner of the canvas (the buggy `labelLayer.text(r)...center(0,0)` and duplicate legend `text(...)` calls create ghost 'next/key/prev' and 'L1/L2/free' labels at the origin) — visible as an illegible smudge that does not exist in the source.
A color legend swatch row ('L1 / L2 / free') has been added under the head boxes; the source has no legend, and its labels are rendered very small (~7px effective) and nearly unreadable.

Overall figure scale: the drawing is rendered at roughly 44% of its design size inside the viewport, so the column indices, key subscripts (k₁…k₉) and row labels are noticeably smaller/lighter than the bold, large serif type of the source.

The white dotted strike-through rules over the free slots' key/prev rows are drawn only as a thin dashed line at the top edge of each free cell; in the source they are thick, prominent dotted rules spanning the cell width at both row boundaries, giving a much stronger 'meaningless entry' cue.
Head boxes for L1/L2 carry a thin gray outline stroke and the panel columns are slightly more widely gapped than the source's tight cell packing — minor proportion/styling drift.
evaluation.notes: Array-based multiple-list table (CLRS Fig 10.7) is reproduced accurately in data, shading and layout with an excellent set of meaningful interactions (step player, chain tracing, allocate/free), but stray ghost text at the canvas origin, an added tiny legend, and the small rendered scale hurt label legibility and polish.
action_items: Delete the two dead `text(...).center(0,0).amove ? null : null` code paths in the row-label and legend loops that leave duplicate glyphs stacked at the top-left corner.
Enlarge the drawing (tighten the viewBox to the actual content bounds, e.g. trim the ~150px right/bottom margins) so column indices, key subscripts and row labels read comfortably at inline size.
Strengthen the free-slot strike-through rules: draw thick white dotted lines at both the next/key and key/prev boundaries across the full cell width, matching the source's emphasis.
Either remove the added legend or increase its font size and align it so it does not read as clutter beside the head boxes.

feedback.rationale: Concept, data, and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, no plan action items); the issues are implementation bugs — ghost glyphs at origin, viewBox scale, strike-through styling, and legend clutter — all fixable in generation.

Head-box labels (free, L2, L1) and their boxes are proportionally smaller relative to the table than in the source, where the head boxes are roughly the height of a table row and visually weighty.

Make the white dotted strike rules span the full cell width with the same heavy dash weight as the source, and thicken/vary the NIL slash strokes (match prev[3]'s opposite diagonal) for exact glyph fidelity.

Legend/annotation strip mapping shade → structure: light gray = L1, medium gray = L2, black = free list

interactions.teaches: That three independent linked structures are interleaved across the same index range: following one head pointer through its next fields visits only its own shade, skipping over slots owned by the other lists.
That a number inside a next or prev cell is not data but an index — hovering lights up the column it points at (or marks it nil), making the pointer semantics of the compact table explicit.
That ALLOCATE-OBJECT pops the head of the free chain and FREE-OBJECT pushes a slot back, so records are never copied — only next, key, and prev entries and the head pointers change.
interactions.label: Allocate / Free

interactions.teaches: That the same free slot can be recycled into either list, showing that ownership is expressed purely by which list's pointers reach it.
interactions.label: Insert allocated slot into

demo_steps.title: One table, three structures
demo_steps.narration: The black panel is a single set of parallel arrays indexed 1 to 10. Shading is the only thing distinguishing three separate structures living inside it: light gray for L1, medium gray for L2, and black for the free list.

demo_steps.title: Trace L1
demo_steps.narration: Click the L1 head box (3): the trace lights slot 3, then next[3]=6, then next[6]=2, then nil. The chain jumps over slots 4 and 5 because those belong to other structures.

demo_steps.title: Trace L2 and read prev
demo_steps.narration: Click L2 (head 9) to follow 9 → 7 → 1 → 5 → nil, then hover any prev cell to see the backward arrow: prev[1]=7 points exactly where next[7]=1 came from, confirming the list is doubly linked.

demo_steps.title: The free list needs only one link
demo_steps.narration: Click the free head (10) to follow 10 → 4 → 8 → nil. The key and prev rows of these slots are struck out with dotted rules — a free slot carries no data and needs no back pointer.

demo_steps.title: Allocate a slot
demo_steps.narration: Press allocate: slot 10 is popped off the free chain, free is reset to 4, and slot 10 is spliced onto the front of L1 — only next[10], prev[3], key[10] and the two head pointers change color and value.

demo_steps.title: Free it again
demo_steps.narration: Press free: slot 10 is unlinked from L1, its key and prev are struck out again, next[10] is set to the old free head, and free points back at 10. No record ever moved in memory.

plan.keyInsight: An 'object' here is nothing but an index — so allocation and deallocation are just relinking next pointers between a shaded list and the free chain, and multiple lists can coexist in one array because shading (ownership) is defined entirely by which chain reaches a slot.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Horizontal layout: a narrow left column of three stacked head-pointer boxes (free = black box with white 10, L2 = medium-gray box with 9, L1 = light-gray box with 3, each with an italic serif label to its left), and a wide black array panel to the right. Above the panel, column indices 1–10 in plain serif numerals. Down the panel's left edge, italic labels next, key, prev for the three rows. Cells are tall narrow rectangles; occupied cells are filled light gray (L1: 3, 6, 2) or medium gray (L2: 9, 7, 1, 5) with dark text; free slots (4, 8, 10) stay black with white text and only a next value, their key/prev cells crossed by dotted white horizontal rules. Nil is drawn as a diagonal slash matching the cell's text color. Keys render as k with a subscript index. Highlight state should use a saturated accent (e.g. orange/amber) outline plus curved arrows arcing above the table from a next cell to the top of the target column, and below the table for prev. Keep the overall tone grayscale so that the accent color reads as 'currently traced'.

discrepancies: Head-box column is compressed against the table: in the source the free / L2 / L1 boxes sit well to the left with generous whitespace, while here the L2 box nearly touches the italic 'key' row label and the L1 box the 'prev' label, making that region look cramped.

The 'free' head box is vertically aligned with the column-index header row rather than floating clearly above/left of the table as in the source, so the three head boxes read as a tighter stack than the original's spread-out arrangement.

Slash (NIL) marks are drawn as uniform straight strokes with only slight variation; the source's slashes differ more visibly in weight/slope (notably the heavier white slash in next[8]) — a cosmetic but visible difference.
The step-narration and legend panel occupies nearly 40% of the frame, shrinking the table relative to the source's full-width composition (default screenshot reads smaller than the original).
evaluation.notes: A faithful reproduction of the CLRS multiple-array/free-list figure with correct values, shading ownership, NIL slashes and dotted strike rules, backed by genuinely useful interactions (chain tracing, allocate/free, 6-step demo); main weaknesses are cramped spacing between the head boxes and row labels and a somewhat shrunken table relative to the source composition.
